title: performance canary: adaptive auto-detection + rollout guards (multi-metric hysteresis)
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Improves performance canary detection by adding multi-metric adaptive thresholds, hysteresis to reduce flapping, tighter rollout guards and better observability for KV cache pressure. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: We observed noisy canary signals from single-threshold detectors causing spurious rollbacks and alert fatigue. This PR introduces an adaptive multi-metric detection engine and a rollout guard state machine that combines p95 latency, tail latency slope, and throughput regression signals with hysteresis and minimum evaluation windows to reduce false positives.

What this changes (summary):
- New detection pipeline (perf_canary/detector) that computes adaptive thresholds from baseline distributions and applies per-metric hysteresis.
- Multi-metric scoring: p95 latency, 99th percentile slope, throughput drop, and KV-cache pressure (cache_miss_rate).
- Rollout guard FSM that requires sustained violation for configurable windows and supports graceful partial rollbacks (traffic step-down) before full rollback.
- Autoscaler integration: detector can mark a canary as "capacity-bound" to trigger autoscaling suggestions instead of rollback.
- Observability: new canary metrics (canary_score, canary_signal_{latency,throughput,kv_miss}), dashboards and tracing tags.
- Test harness: synthetic workload generator + perf-canary lab tests to validate sensitivity and hysteresis tuning.

Checklist:
- [x] Detection engine and FSM implemented
- [x] Unit + integration tests for detector logic
- [x] Load tests in perf-canary lab (1000 runs)
- [x] Dashboards and alert rules updated
- [x] Docs updated (perf-canary README + runbook)

Notes on safety: Default hysteresis and thresholds are conservative. The new logic is behind a feature flag (perf_canary.v2) and rollout will start with internal accounts only. We expect negligible runtime overhead (instrumentation added to existing path; heavy work runs in background evaluation loop).

Related: ENG-1987 (reduce false positives), ENG-2034 (canary autoscaler integration), SUP-4123 (customer incident motivated tuning).

observations: Perf lab summary: 1000 synthetic runs across small/medium/large models. Median p95 regression detection latency reduced; false positives dropped. CPU overhead ~1.4% on evaluator worker, memory +5MB per route for baseline buffers.
ci_summary: Initial CI: lint fail, flaky perf test failure. Final CI: all checks passed (unit, integration, perf-lab, e2e).
backout_plan: Revert feature flag perf_canary.v2, route traffic back to v1 detector. Run revert script services/perf-canary/revert_v2.sh and rollback dashboard alerts. Documented in runbook.
test_plan: Unit tests (detector logic), integration tests (end-to-end evaluation FSM), perf-lab (1000 runs replaying historical traces), canary rollout to internal orgs then gradual expansion.
impact_analysis: No API changes. Operationally, fewer spurious rollbacks and less alert fatigue expected. Potential risk: new detector could suppress legitimate signals if misconfigured; mitigated by conservative defaults and manual override.
